heroLead: Clarington sits on the Ohio River in southern Monroe County, one of the most consistently strong-producing counties in the entire Utica play.
intro: If your family owns minerals near Clarington, you're in a part of the state where operators have reported some of the highest initial production rates anywhere in the Utica formation. That doesn't automatically translate into a specific number for your tract, but it does mean the surrounding activity gives a buyer plenty of comparable data to work from, whether or not your own parcel has a well on it yet.
Monroe County's population is small and rural, which means courthouse research in Woodsfield can be a more hands-on process than in a busier county, but the underlying title work is no different.

sections.heading: River-town land history
paragraphs: Clarington's location on the Ohio River gave it an early role in regional trade and industry, and some mineral severances here trace back to that period, sometimes tied to riverfront or landing-related transactions rather than a simple farm deed. A title search at the Monroe County Recorder's office will clarify whether your family's tract has this kind of layered history.

sections.heading: Strong core-play numbers nearby
paragraphs: Wells throughout Monroe County have posted some of the strongest production figures in the state, and Clarington-area acreage sits well within that core. If your tract is part of an active spacing unit, your division order and recent royalty statements are the clearest way to establish real value.

sections.heading: If your family's minerals were never leased
paragraphs: Given how much activity has moved through this part of Monroe County, it's worth double-checking whether your specific tract was ever offered a lease, since paperwork on older, unleased parcels sometimes gets separated from a family's other records over the years. If it genuinely hasn't been leased, an offer will be built from nearby comparable activity rather than existing production.

faqs.question: Is Monroe County a strong part of the Utica play?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's consistently posted some of the highest per-well production figures anywhere in the play.

faqs.question: My family's Clarington property has river-related deed history. Does that complicate title?
faqs.answer: It can add older transactions to trace, so a full title search is worthwhile rather than assuming a standard rural chain of title applies.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my unleased tract was ever offered a lease?
faqs.answer: A search at the Monroe County Recorder's office will show any lease ever recorded against your legal description, even if the paperwork in your own family's files has been lost.
